Subject: GPU docking availability verification — UnityCorp (UCP-4382)

Ben / Marissa —

We're moving to final commercial terms with UnityCorp (deal UCP-4382). They expect a production start in ~6–8 weeks and have asked for a provisional capacity hold to ensure predictable latency for their LLM inference (primary model: 8x H100-class equivalent, target sustained 50 rps for 4k context).

Ask: can ops confirm whether we can provision a provisional docking of 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (or the A100-equivalent quantized profile we discussed) in our us-west fleet for a 30-day soft-hold window starting as early as 2029-05-15? If not, what minimum commit / sizing would ensure the SLA?

Notes: UnityCorp procurement is sensitive to lead time. I've attached the MOP answers they submitted. They are preferring a soft-hold with a documented MAP rather than a contractual reserve for now.

If we can get an internal availability snapshot and a recommended hold cadence (soft-hold vs firm reserve + fallback variants), I will relay to Chris and lock the timeline.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: unitycorp-mop-answers.xlsx

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 May 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU docking availability verification — UnityCorp (UCP-4382)

Laura —

Thanks for the context and the MOP. Quick inventory snapshot for us-west pool (as of 2029-05-01 10:45 PDT):

- H100-equivalents available: 6 dedicated nodes (each node = 1x H100-equivalent partition)
- A100-equivalents available: 28 partitions (can be grouped to emulate H100 throughput with quantized profile)
- Idle burst capacity (non-reserved): typically 15–20 partitions but varies by day; last week we saw a 48-hour contention window on build nights.

What I recommend:
1) Soft-hold: place a 30-day provisional soft-hold for 8 H100-equivalent capacity using A100-quantized profile as fallback. We can allocate 6 H100-equiv native and 2 from grouped A100s; this would be flagged as "soft-hold: pending PO" in the system.
2) Contingency: if traffic spikes beyond 65 rps, auto-fallback to cross-region burst (us-east) with an additional latency delta of ~15–20ms.
3) Ops ticket + runbook: I will attach a fleet map (fleet-map-v2.pdf) and open a provisioning ticket. We need confirmation of preferred start date and whether they require a hard SLA (commit) or are okay with soft-hold + MAP.

I will also flag the potential contention window on 2029-05-22 to 2029-05-24 based on current reservations — if they need strict isolation, we should push for a firm commit.

--
Ben Carter
Capacity Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: fleet-map-v2.pdf

From: Chris Taylor <chris.taylor@unitycorp.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU docking availability verification — UnityCorp (UCP-4382)

Laura —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying points from our side:

- UnityCorp prefers H100-equivalent performance for the first 90 days of production to validate latency-sensitive features. We understand a soft-hold is common; can Redwood provide a 30-day provisional window and then convert to a short-term reserved commit if we sign PO within that window?
- We can accept cross-region fallback for bursts if the latency impact is clearly documented.
- Proposed start date: 2029-05-20, pending internal sign-off; procurement expects to issue a PO no later than 2029-06-05 if terms are acceptable.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can create a provisional hold with the option to convert to reserved capacity upon receipt of PO? Also please share any required lead times to convert to firm reserved capacity.

Thanks —
Chris Taylor
Senior Platform Engineer, UnityCorp
chris.taylor@unitycorp.com

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Chris Taylor <chris.taylor@unitycorp.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU docking availability verification — UnityCorp (UCP-4382)

Chris —

We can do exactly that. Proposed approach:

- Redwood will create a 30-day provisional soft-hold starting 2029-05-20 for 8 H100-equivalent GPUs in us-west, with an explicit conversion path to a 3-month reserved commit upon PO receipt.
- Conversion lead time: operationally we can convert from provisional to reserved within 48–72 hours after PO confirmation; if you require hard isolation we recommend reserving the full commit as early as possible.
- Fallback: cross-region burst to us-east if utilization exceeds the soft-hold allocation; expected additional p99 latency +15–25ms (we'll include an empirical latency baseline).

Next steps: I will ask Ben to open the soft-hold ticket and attach the provisional MAP. If you confirm the start date and expected PO window (target 2029-06-05), we'll proceed.

Best —
Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
